Theme

Latin word

Paraclītus

Paraclītus, Paraclītī m.

noun, second declension

the Paraclete, the Comforter

In this lexicon

  • the Holy Spirit

    also used · late Latin · Vulg. Jo. 14.26

Notes

  1. 1Paraclītus: spelled with ī (Lewis & Short paraclētus). The Clementine Vulgate’s and the Roman Breviary’s spelling (Jo. 14.26), from Greek παράκλητος with η said as ī; the Stuttgart Vulgate prints paraclētus (Latinitas Precēs, Notae).

Examples

  • Paraclītus autem Spīritus Sānctus, quem mittet Pater in nōmine meō, ille vōs docēbit omnia

    But the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all thingsVulg. Jo. 14.26

    In the entry for the Holy Spirit
